title: Why Your Car Insurance Keeps Going Up (Even With No Accidents)
alts: Car Insurance Up 50% in 5 Years? Here's Who Sets Your Price
No Accidents, Higher Bill: Why Car Insurance Keeps Rising
line1: Why does your car insurance keep going up when you never crash? Prices rose ~50% in 5 years. Here's where your money really goes.
summary: Dave has a clean record, yet his renewal jumps from $1,800 to $2,200. We explain how insurance pools risk (the village pot from our insurance episode), why car insurance rose about 50% in five years versus 22% for everything else (BLS CPI), how sensors and cameras turned bumpers into $2,000 repairs (AAA), bigger crashes, distracted driving and rising injury payouts (NHTSA, CCC), record storm losses (Triple-I), ZIP code pricing, credit-based insurance scores, and the loyalty penalty known as price optimization. Then how to fight back: shop every renewal, raise your deductible carefully, bundle, and weigh telematics.
learn: Why you pay for everyone's crashes, not just your own (how insurance pools risk)
How car insurance rose ~50% in 5 years while prices overall rose ~22% (BLS CPI)
Why sensors, radar and cameras make small repairs cost thousands
How storms, your ZIP code and your credit score change your price
What price optimization and the loyalty penalty are, and where they're restricted
How to lower your car insurance: shop at renewal, deductible, bundling, telematics (education, not advice)
